1.explanation: Both the un-minified and minified JavaScript language definition files carry the logic for recognizing regex literals, comments, and template literals (including their opening and closing backticks). The bug report shows broken template-literal parsing only in JavaScript highlighting, so these are the files that need to be corrected. Adjusting the regex or lookbehind rules in prism-javascript.js (and then rebuilding or re-minifying) will fix the stray open 'template-punctuation' span.
1.bug_scenario: In the user’s screenshot you can see that after parsing a regex literal that contains a single-quote (replace(/'/, `'`)) and then a normal template literal in a comment, the very next vanilla template literal (`const var3 = `break starts here`;`) is not closed properly by the highlighter. Prism opens a when it sees the backtick, highlights the contents as expected, but never emits the closing ``. As a result the remainder of the file (including var4) is all swallowed into that open span.

2.explanation: The JavaScript grammar is defined in prism-javascript.js (and its minified counterpart). That file contains the ‘template-string’ token and the look-behind logic for interpolation. The bug manifests as an off-by-one in the open/close regex for backtick strings (and interactions with single-quote regexes and comments), so fixing the ‘template-string’ pattern in prism-javascript.js will resolve the broken highlighting. The minified file must also be regenerated once the fix is applied.
2.bug_scenario:
When Prism highlights JavaScript source containing a regex literal with single-quotes inside template literals, followed by a backtick comment, any subsequent ordinary template literals are not closed properly. In the reproducer you see

1. A replace(/'/, `'`) call is highlighted correctly.
2. A comment containing backticks (// `load bearing comment`) is parsed and highlighted correctly.
3. But the very next template string (`break starts here`) never closes its <span> and “steals” highlighting until end of file (var3 and var4 remain green/span open).
